Mauritius Reels as Cyclone Emelda Batters Island; Economic Disruption Spreads

PORT LOUIS, Mauritius, June 17 – Mauritius remained on high alert Monday as Cyclone Emelda continued to lash the Indian Ocean island, causing widespread disruption to transport, business operations, and key infrastructure. The Mauritius Meteorological Services reported sustained winds of up to 140 kilometers per hour and heavy rainfall, with flash flooding reported in Port Louis and several coastal towns.

Thousands of homes have lost power, and authorities warned that restoration efforts could take days as strong winds hamper repair crews. The government has closed all schools and non-essential offices, urging residents to remain indoors. The main airport and seaports have suspended operations since Sunday night, stranding travelers and halting cargo shipments.

The economic impact is already being felt across multiple sectors. Azure Power Global Ltd, which operates solar facilities and supports Mauritius’s renewable energy supply, confirmed that several of its installations in the central plateau region have been temporarily shut down due to storm damage and safety concerns. “Our teams are working closely with emergency services to assess the situation and resume safe operations as soon as possible,” said a company spokesperson in a statement.

The Mauritius Chamber of Commerce and Industry warned of “significant short-term disruption” to supply chains and exports, noting that many businesses have suspended operations. “This is a critical time for small and medium enterprises,” said Chamber president Jean-Luc Renaud. “The cyclone’s impact on logistics, energy, and communications is likely to be severe.”

Local authorities have deployed emergency teams to clear blocked roads and assist affected residents, but interior regions remain difficult to access. The Red Cross Mauritius reported that evacuation centers are nearing capacity in flood-prone communities.

The cyclone is expected to continue affecting Mauritius through Tuesday, with further heavy rainfall and wind damage anticipated.
